title: Harmfulness Gradient: Does Incremental Escalation of Harmful Content in Fine-Tuning Data Produce a Threshold Effect?

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Exceptionally actionable: determining the dose-response curve shape (linear vs threshold) for harmful data in fine-tuning directly informs data-filtering thresholds for fine-tuning APIs. If a threshold exists, small amounts of harmful data may be safe.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Fine-tuning Llama-3-8B with varying data mixes is doable with HuggingFace tools. However, creating/sourcing synthetic harmful instruction datasets and running 6 fine-tuning runs on an 8B model requires medium-to-high compute and careful data preparation.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Six fine-tuning runs at different harmful data fractions, plus ASR measurement at each, plus curve fitting. Each 8B fine-tuning run takes substantial time. 20 hours is optimistic. Tight for 30 hours but potentially feasible with efficient setup.
